maya: Heads-up — noticed a reproducible p99 tail in streaming chat when microbatch size > 8. Non-streaming completions with the same mb_size look fine.

sidharth: rough numbers?

maya: dev cluster, g4x2, baseline mb=4 p50/95/99 = 18/55/120ms. mb=12 -> 20/110/420ms for streaming chat (p99 spikes). non-streaming: 22/95/130ms (no huge tail).

eric: interesting. do we see kernel switch/fallback in traces?

maya: yes — kernel selector flips to the long-seq fallback kernel at certain sequence lengths when we pack multiple chat streams. stacktrace shows kernel A -> kernel B on iteration 3.

julia: is KV cache miss pattern different for streaming? streaming tends to have smaller incremental tokens but more frequent KV access churn. maybe KV eviction/warmup causing stalls.

maya: attaching a short perf dump: ```
# perf summary
name kernelA kernelB kv_hit_rate queue_ms
mb4   0.82   0.18    0.94       6
mb12  0.43   0.57    0.66      48
```

maya: also saw queueing microbursts in the controller logs: `queueing_latency_samples: [2,3,5,200,4]` when mb=12.

sidharth: that 200ms looks like a tail from a single request blocking the batch. could be KV cache miss that triggers a fallback path and stalls the batch.

eric: do we know which requests in the batch caused the fallback? can we correlate to prompt lengths / system messages?

maya: yes — correlated to mixed-length history. chat requests with longer histories push cumulative seq > 1024 and kernel selector picks B. With batching, one long history forces kernelB for entire batch. streaming clients exacerbate this because they append tokens gradually and keep small mb yet mixed lengths.

julia: idea: change batcher heuristic to split by "kernel_compatibility_key" that includes estimated seq_len. then ensure batches are homogeneous for kernel choice. That should avoid long-tail forced kernel switches.

sidharth: good. tradeoff: smaller homogeneous batches -> lower throughput. need SLO guardrails: streaming SLOs (p95/p99) prioritized, completions maximize throughput.

eric: propose timeline: (1) quick heuristic change to avoid mixing long histories in same batch for streaming (2) prewarm KV cache for clients with repeated chat sessions (3) run canary with mb_streaming=6, mb_nonstream=16.

maya: I can prototype the kernel_compat_key split today. measurement target: p99 drop to <200ms for streaming, throughput drop <10%.

julia: small nit: ensure the batcher emits `batch_meta.kv_estimate` so kernel selection can be hinted earlier (avoid compute-heavy kernel probe inside hot path).

sidharth: also check kernel hinting flags — we can set `prefer_fast_kernel=true` for batches where all seq_est <= 512. that will bias selection. fallback still allowed but less likely.

perf-bot: benchmark run queued: `bench/streaming_mb12_vs_mb6/2741592000`

perf-bot: results (canary): streaming mb=6 p99=160ms, throughput -8%; streaming mb=12 p99=420ms, throughput baseline. non-streaming mb=16 p99=140ms, throughput +18%

eric: looks promising. streaming mb=6 keeps tail under control.

julia: next action: add policy to route streaming chat to smaller target mb by default and bump non-streaming to larger mb. Also add batcher split by `kernel_compat_key`.

maya: I'll open a PR with the batcher split and an env flag `STREAMING_TARGET_MB=6` so ops can tune per-region.

sidharth: we'll want tracing: add span tags `chosen_kernel` and `batch_reason` and emit `kv_miss_count` per batch.

eric: ops: can we roll the canary to prod with a 1% traffic guard for 24h? watch p99 and tail events.

julia: yes, we should also add a regression alert: if streaming p99 > 300ms for 5m, auto-roll back routing to previous mb.

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4823 (draft) — includes tests and perf harness.

sidharth: tests to add: synthetic chest workloads with mixed history lengths, KV cold-start simulation, and kernel-switch trace assertions.

eric: thanks — big win if we can keep streaming SLO strict and not sacrifice completions throughput. Small follow-ups: quantify cost delta for more small batches, and update docs for recommended per-workload mb configs.

maya: will run cost calc after PR merges. tagging you all for review. :rocket:

julia: thanks — will review today. :thumbsup:
